extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for claiming foreign priority under 37 CFR 1.55: timing for filing certified copies or interim copies, use of the Priority Document Exchange (PDX), required content/format of documents, translation requirements, remedies for late filing, and examiner handling of priority papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing certified copy (37 CFR 1.55(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: For an original application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) filed on or after March 16, 2013, a certified copy of the foreign application must be filed within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the (U.S.) application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application. For international applications entering the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, the certified copy must be filed within the time limits set forth by the PCT, with specific later-of periods if not filed during the international stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time period does not apply to design applications. If a certified copy is not filed within these periods and none of the exceptions apply (see 37 CFR 1.55(h),(i),(j)), the certified copy must be accompanied by a petition showing good and sufficient cause and the petition fee per § 1.17(g). If certified copy is filed after payment of the issue fee the patent will not include the priority claim unless corrected by a certificate of correction (35 U.S.C. 255; 37 CFR 1.323).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to time requirement (37 CFR 1.55(h),(i),(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing time requirement of 37 CFR 1.55(f) does not apply if: (1) a prior-filed nonprovisional application for which benefit is claimed contains and is identified as containing a certified copy of the foreign application (37 CFR 1.55(h)); (2) the priority application was filed in a participating foreign intellectual property office or a copy was filed in a subsequently-filed application in a participating office and the Office receives the copy during pendency and before grant (37 CFR 1.55(i)); or (3) the applicant provides an interim copy and later files the certified copy during pendency (37 CFR 1.55(j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each exception has its own procedural requirements (see individual entries). Applicants should identify when an exception applies and follow the corresponding procedural steps to avoid petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Document Exchange (PDX) satisfies timeliness (37 CFR 1.55(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to file a certified copy within the 1.55(f) time limits will be considered satisfied if the foreign application was filed in a foreign IP office participating in a bilateral/multilateral priority document exchange agreement (or a copy was filed in a subsequent application in such an office), the priority claim is presented in an application data sheet identifying the foreign application (application number, country, day, month, year), and the copy is received by the USPTO from the participating office within the specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can use Form PTO/SB/38 (Request to Retrieve Electronic Priority Application(s)) to request retrieval. USPTO attempts retrieval when the application is docketed to an examiner and will not attempt electronic retrieval until OAP processing is complete; successful retrieval takes approximately one week but is not guaranteed. Applicants remain ultimately responsible for ensuring receipt of the priority document during pendency and before grant and are encouraged to check Patent Center for retrieval status. If the foreign application was not filed in a participating office but a copy exists in a subsequent application filed in a participating office, a separate request identifying the subsequent application must be filed within the relevant time period or accompanied by a petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim copy permitted to satisfy timeliness (37 CFR 1.55(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ‘interim copy’ of the original foreign application, clearly labeled 'Interim Copy', including specification and any drawings or claims, together with a separate cover sheet identifying the foreign application (application number, country, day, month, year) and stating the copy is a true copy as filed, may be filed to satisfy the time requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interim copy and cover sheet must be filed within the later of sixteen months from the prior foreign filing or four months from the U.S. filing (or corresponding national stage dates) or with an appropriate petition. A certified copy still must be filed within the period specified in 37 CFR 1.55(g)(1) (unless accompanied by an appropriate petition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents and labeling of interim copy
rubrics_metrics.description: The interim copy must be clearly labeled as 'Interim Copy,' include the specification and any drawings or claims upon which it is based, and be accompanied by a separate cover sheet identifying the foreign application by application number, country (or IP authority), day, month, and year of filing, and stating that the copy filed is a true copy of the original foreign application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing via USPTO electronic filing, applicants should select the document description 'Interim Copy of the Foreign Priority Application' to index the document. Parts submitted only as plain text (.txt) should be filed as text files and indexed appropriately ('Interim Copy of the Foreign Priority (text file)'). XML parts (e.g., ST.26 sequence listings) may be filed on a read-only optical disc as part of the interim copy. See MPEP § 502.05 and related sections for electronic filing details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted file formats and indexing for interim copy
rubrics_metrics.description: If not provided as a single paper document, the main parts of an interim copy (Abstract, Drawings, Specification, Claims, sequence listings, large tables, program listings) may be filed as a single PDF image file via USPTO electronic filing, or as .txt for plain text parts, or as XML on a read-only optical disc for XML parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing online, select the appropriate document description to index each part. The PDF image file will be stored in the file wrapper and must be indexed as 'Interim Copy of the Foreign Priority Application' (or appropriate text/XML description).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form PTO/SB/38 to request retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can use Form PTO/SB/38 (Request to Retrieve Electronic Priority Application(s)) to request that the Office obtain a copy of the foreign application from a participating intellectual property office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate written request is required when the foreign application is not originally filed in a participating office but a certified copy was filed in an application subsequently filed in a participating office. Requests must identify the participating office and the subsequent application's number and filing date and be filed within the relevant time window or accompanied by a petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibility to ensure receipt and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants continue to bear the ultimate responsibility for ensuring that the priority document is filed during the pendency of the application and before the patent is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDX retrieval is not guaranteed; applicants are encouraged to check Patent Center to confirm receipt. If the Office does not receive a copy through PDX in time, the applicant must file a certified copy or appropriate petition to preserve priority entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and remedies for late or improper filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a certified copy is not filed within the specified time and no exception applies, the certified copy must be accompanied by a petition showing good and sufficient cause for the delay and the fee in § 1.17(g). A certified copy filed after payment of the issue fee will not result in the patent including the priority claim unless corrected by a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and 37 CFR 1.323 (and, where applicable, a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.55(e) if unintentionally delayed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An improper, incomplete, or inconsistent citation of a foreign priority application will delay or prevent retrieval under PDX; applicants are strongly encouraged to cite the foreign application using an acceptable format and to use proper and consistent citation format throughout the U.S. application. The provision for belated filing under 1.55(f) is a lower standard/fee than petitions under 1.183.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Office may require earlier filing of priority papers (37 CFR 1.55(g)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require that the claim for priority and the certified copy be filed earlier than otherwise provided when: (A) the application is involved in an interference or derivation proceeding; (B) when necessary to overcome the date of an interference or a reference relied upon by the examiner; or (C) when deemed necessary by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required earlier, the certified copy must be furnished by the date specified. Failure to provide required papers timely may affect prosecution and patentability. See cited MPEP sections for form paragraphs and examiner practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for non-English foreign applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An English-language translation of a non-English foreign application is not generally required, except when: (i) the application is involved in an interference or derivation proceeding; (ii) necessary to overcome the date of a reference relied upon by the examiner; or (iii) specifically required by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a translation is required, it must be a translation of the certified copy of the foreign application and must be filed together with a statement that the translation of the certified copy is accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners' review of priority papers and entitlement to priority
rubrics_metrics.description: When the claim and certified copy are received while the application is pending before the examiner, the examiner generally only checks for obvious formal defects and correspondence in number, date, and country with the application data sheet (or oath/declaration). The subject matter is not examined to determine entitlement to the priority date unless required for patentability reasons (e.g., intervening reference, interference/derivation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an intervening reference is found that raises priority entitlement issues, the examiner may reject claims and then require the foreign papers or translations to be filed to overcome the reference; form paragraphs (e.g., 2.19) may be used to request translation or further papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper citation format and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: An improper, incomplete, or inconsistent citation of a foreign priority application and/or its filing date will result in delay or prevent retrieval under the PDX program; any incomplete foreign priority claim will prevent successful electronic retrieval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly encouraged to cite the foreign application using an acceptable format (see MPEP § 214.04) and to use proper and consistent citation format throughout the U.S. application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical filing suggestion: annotate priority papers with U.S. application number
rubrics_metrics.description: It is suggested that the notation of the application number of the corresponding U.S. application be placed on the priority papers when such papers are not submitted via a PDX program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the notation directly on the priority papers themselves (not just on a cover letter) to avoid separation of papers and cover letters, which causes difficulty correlating priority papers with the corresponding U.S. application.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDX and WIPO DAS specifics for design and PCT applications
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO will attempt retrieval of foreign applications to which priority is claimed in a U.S. design application where possible. The Spanish PTO deposits certain ES industrial design applications for USPTO access via WIPO DAS. USPTO will automatically attempt retrieval of PCT international applications where the receiving office is RO/AU, RO/DK, RO/ES, RO/FI, RO/IB, RO/MA or RO/SE and the applicant has provided the required WIPO DAS access code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants claiming priority to such foreign or international applications should provide WIPO DAS access codes and identify the foreign applications properly on the application data sheet to enable automated retrieval.
